ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows toothpick patterns numbered 1, 2, and 3 in order: Pattern 1 is a 1×1 small square enclosed by toothpicks; Pattern 2 is a 2×2 square grid, sharing adjacent sides; Pattern 3 is a 3×3 square grid, sharing adjacent sides. Therefore it can be inferred that the nth pattern is an n×n toothpick square grid. Reasoning: In the nth pattern, in the horizontal direction there are n+1 horizontal layers in total, and each layer has n toothpicks, so there are n(n+1) horizontal toothpicks; in the vertical direction, similarly there are n(n+1) vertical toothpicks. Therefore the total number of toothpicks T(n)=2n(n+1). The number of toothpicks increased from the 30th pattern to the 31st pattern is T(31)-T(30)=2·31·32-2·30·31=1984-1860=124.
